claims.text: Healthy infants: routine bronchodilators (eg, albuterol), hypertonic saline and abx are ⍉recommended;
claims.quote: Evidence-based guidelines recommend against routine use of bronchodilators (eg, albuterol), hypertonic saline, and antibiotics in otherwise healthy infants
Furthermore, corticosteroids have been demonstrated to be ineffective for typical bronchiolitis.

claims.text: Bronchodilators aren't universally effective, but a trial of aerosolized albuterol may be considered, esp w severe resp compromise.
claims.quote: Although bronchodilators are not universally effective, a trial of aerosolized albuterol may be considered, especially for infants with severe respiratory compromise.

claims.text: Aerosolized ribavirin: rarely used, reserved for select immunocompromised pts.
claims.quote: aerosolized ribavirin, approved for severe RSV in the 1980s, is rarely used today due to limited efficacy, administration challenges, and safety concerns, and remains reserved for select immunocompromised patients.

claims.text: RSV prev: long-acting mAbs (nirsevimab, clesrovimab) give ~5 mo of protection and ↓RSV hospitalizations;
claims.quote: Additionally, long-acting monoclonal antibodies, including nirsevimab and the recently approved clesrovimab, confer approximately 5 months of protection and significantly reduce RSV-related hospitalizations.
Monthly palivizumab prophylaxis was discontinued in 2025 due to the superior convenience of long-acting agents.
